findings.evidence: 'Leaving `[NEEDS CLARIFICATION]` unflagged | Unresolved ambiguity marker -> HIGH' repeats line 122 ('Unresolved ambiguity markers left in') and line 171 ('ambiguity_markers ... any left unresolved -> HIGH'). The checklists also carry generic review items the model already knows, e.g. line 116 'Not testable — fast, user-friendly, robust' and line 148 'circular dependencies; wrong execution order'. Lines 22-24 (Workflow) and 92-95 (Phase 2) are only pointers.
findings.fix: State each rule once: keep the ambiguity-marker rule in Framework conventions (line 171) and remove the restatements at lines 122 and 330. Merge the Workflow and Phase 2 pointer paragraphs into the section headings. Cut generic checklist wording down to the severity tier it sets (for example 'untestable requirement -> HIGH').

findings.evidence: '## Phase 2 — Apply the checklist' has only two lines. The rules applied during it (Codebase grounding at line 183, Linter-silencing at 211, budget at 216, Tool preference at 240) sit between Phase 2 and Phase 3 with no step saying when each one fires. The legacy-tool rule is split between line 155 and line 255.
findings.fix: Turn Phase 2 into ordered steps: (a) read SHARED_TOOLING_PATH and TOOL_AVAILABILITY if given, (b) ground every factual claim (Codebase grounding), (c) apply the archetype checklist(s) and profile conventions, (d) apply the linter-silencing and legacy-tool rules. Under headless dispatch, print findings inline as you go. Keep the legacy-tool rule in one place.

findings.evidence: Common Mistakes rows without a reason: 'Ignoring the framework's requirement syntax | A non-EARS Kiro requirement / SHALL-less OpenSpec requirement is a real finding.' and 'Reviewing a constitution/state doc as if it were a spec | Those are context — read, don't review.' The table never says why.
findings.fix: Give each row a reason, for example: 'the framework's own tooling and downstream steps parse that syntax, so a non-EARS clause is not generated into tests', and 'reviewing STATE/constitution docs produces findings no fixer can act on, which blocks Approved forever'.

findings.evidence: The description has WHAT, WHEN and strong keywords but no boundary against its close neighbours (ai-kit-spec-review-fixer, the /ai-kit-spec-review loop, code or PR review). It spends words on mechanics ('Accepts a pre-resolved FRAMEWORK_PROFILE_PATH + ARCHETYPE ... falls back to its own framework detection') rather than on user intent, and has no 'even without the word' clause.
findings.fix: Audit a spec-driven-development document (intent, requirements, design or plan) with a severity-rated checklist plus its framework's own rules (EARS/SHALL syntax, Given/When/Then, OpenSpec deltas, Spec Kit [NEEDS CLARIFICATION] and [P] markers, constitutional gates). Detects superpowers, OpenSpec, Spec Kit, Kiro, BMAD and GSD layouts; else generic. Use when a design doc, spec, PRD, requirements.md, tasks.md, CONTEXT.md or implementation plan needs a clean-context review before the next step, or to find contradictions, untestable requirements, undefined interfaces or unsafe parallel tasks, even without the words 'spec review'. Accepts FRAMEWORK_PROFILE_PATH and ARCHETYPE from /ai-kit-spec-review. Not for fixing findings or editing the doc (ai-kit-spec-review-fixer), the review-fix loop (/ai-kit-spec-review), or code/PR review.

findings.evidence: The body is 337 lines of long prose lines, an estimated 6,000 tokens, above the about-5,000-token guide. Two sections apply only under a condition but load on every run: '## Operating under a turn/token budget (external CLI dispatch)' (lines 216-238) and '## Tool preference during review' (lines 240-264, needed only when SHARED_TOOLING_PATH or TOOL_AVAILABILITY is present).
findings.fix: Move both sections to references/headless-budget.md and references/tool-preference.md. In Phase 1, add gated reads: 'If you were dispatched through a headless CLI, Read references/headless-budget.md before your first tool call' and 'If a SHARED_TOOLING_PATH or TOOL_AVAILABILITY line is present, Read references/tool-preference.md; otherwise do not load it.'

findings.evidence: 'Trust the archetype — the orchestrator has project context you don't.' This is an unconditional rule with no way out when the passed archetype plainly contradicts the content shape (for example ARCHETYPE = plan on a doc with no tasks). It leads to the 'Plan-level strictness on a design' mistake that line 327 forbids.
findings.fix: Keep the passed archetype as the default and add an escape hatch: 'If the content shape clearly contradicts the passed archetype, still review with it, and add one Non-blocking note naming the mismatch and the archetype the content shape suggests.'

findings.evidence: Every one of the 9 evals expects '### Status: Issues Found' or Failure. None checks the Approved shape, the only-LOW -> Approved with Non-blocking notes rule, the inline-content 'Failure — input not on disk' path, Cross-Document Consistency on two files, or an OpenSpec MODIFIED/REMOVED delta. A reviewer that always reports Issues Found passes the whole set.
findings.fix: Add evals for: a truly clean design (evals/files/design-clean.md) asserting the report ends with '### Status: Approved' and has no severity heading; a doc with only a tooling-catchable LOW issue asserting Approved plus a plain '- <text>' note; an inline-content prompt asserting '### Status: Failure — input not on disk'; and an OpenSpec delta whose MODIFIED entry has no match, asserting a CRITICAL finding.

findings.evidence: The 20 queries are balanced 10/10 with good near-misses, but almost all are terse and lack the realistic context the trigger-query guide asks for (file paths, personal context, typos), e.g. 'review this design doc against the checklist before I write the plan'.
findings.fix: Rewrite 4-5 queries with real context, e.g. 'my lead wants docs/superpowers/specs/2026-11-02-export-design.md sanity-checked before i write the plan, can u look for gaps' and 'openspec/changes/add-csv/specs/export/spec.md — does the MODIFIED block actually match something in the stable spec?'

findings.evidence: Line 13-14: 'The only write allowed is persisting an in-context document to disk verbatim so you can Read it' allows the reviewer to persist inline content itself. Line 28-31: 'If the caller passed inline content or a chat description, STOP: ### Status: Failure — input not on disk. Caller must persist the document and re-invoke with a path.' The two lines disagree on what to do with inline input.
findings.fix: Choose one branch and state it in both places. Either delete the write allowance at line 13-14 ('Never write anything; inline input ends with the Failure status in Phase 1 step 1'), or replace step 1 with 'If given inline content, write it verbatim to <run tmp dir>/<name>.md, Read it back, and list that path under Files Read.'

findings.evidence: 'If the orchestrator passed FRAMEWORK_PROFILE_PATH and ARCHETYPE ... do not proceed with generic checklists while a real profile path was given' gives no outcome when the profile file cannot be read, or when only one of the two lines is present (the Else branch would then re-detect and could ignore the given path).
findings.fix: Add: 'If FRAMEWORK_PROFILE_PATH names a file that cannot be read, end with ### Status: Failure — profile not readable: <path>. If only FRAMEWORK_PROFILE_PATH is given, use that profile and classify the archetype from its doc_types; if only ARCHETYPE is given, use it with the fallback framework detection.'
